literal_source_claim: The L^2 Fourier transform is an isometry.
canonical_claim: For complex-valued square-integrable functions on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, the correctly normalized Fourier transform extends to an L^2 isometry; in particular it preserves the L^2 norm and inner product.
domain_and_universes: Intended scalar domain: complex-valued L2 functions over finite-dimensional real Euclidean space. Exact dimension binder, measure, Fourier character, normalization, and whether the source supports a more general locally compact abelian group remain open.
quantifiers: f in complex L2 on the selected Euclidean space
hypotheses: the Fourier transform and measure use the source-approved compatible normalization
conclusion: The Fourier transform preserves the L2 norm; inner-product preservation is included only after its equivalence under the frozen conventions is checked.
excluded_degenerate_cases: The zero-dimensional space is provisionally included. Infinite-dimensional spaces, arbitrary LCA groups, non-L2 functions, and unnormalized transforms are excluded unless the selected source explicitly changes the scope.
